# Clavis Encrypt 3.14.0

## 🆕 Clavis on a USB stick

- Carry your encrypted files on a USB stick or USB drive and open them on other Windows PCs, without installing anything there. Open **USB Stick** in the sidebar, pick your drive, and press **Set up stick**.
- Clavis copies itself, your vault and your licence onto the drive, plus a page that opens your files in any web browser, for PCs that don't allow programs from USB drives.
- On the other PC, Clavis runs from the drive and keeps everything on it: nothing is installed or left behind on that PC, there's no right-click menu and no activity history there. **Finish and remove stick** (also the window's close button) closes Clavis so you can unplug the drive safely.
- Works with USB sticks, memory cards and portable USB drives (SSDs and hard disks). If Windows has a connected drive switched off, Clavis tells you how to switch it on.
- Setting up and updating a stick is part of **Clavis Pro**. Adding the browser page and repairing a stick are free.
- Your key file and Windows Hello stay on your own PC. Keep your recovery key somewhere other than the stick.

## Also

- **Settings** moved to the bottom of the sidebar, next to About, so every menu item fits.
- The sidebar no longer shows an icon next to Shred Files.

## Install / upgrade

- **Windows, already installed:** the app updates itself (Settings → Updates → Check now), or download the new installer from https://clavisenc.com/download.html.
- **Microsoft Store:** the Store updates it automatically. (The Store version can add the browser page and an Encrypted files folder to a stick; copying the app itself needs the version from clavisenc.com.)
- **Linux:** install the new `.deb` from https://clavisenc.com/download.html.

Your vaults and settings are kept.
